newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power steady as weather moderates.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power steady as weather moderates.

text.p: Warmer temperatures and expectations of rain in the U.S. Northwest helped spot power prices hold steady, market sources said Wednesday.
"This is mainly because of weather, but gas prices are also trending down," said one trader. "Daily (power) prices may stay firm, but December will trail off."
He noted spot power prices are historically lower in December than in November, due in part to the easing of fish-related flow requirements for hydroelectric projects.
According to recent forecasts, the Pacific Northwest will see normal temperatures over the next week or so, while precipitation will be slightly above normal.
The Southwest is expected to have slightly below normal temperatures.
Next-day firm, on-peak quotes for California-Oregon border (COB) power were $24.50-25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), up slightly from Wednesday.
Mid-Columbia was last quoted $22.00-23.00, also unchanged.
Palo Verde firm on-peak power for Thursday was quoted $20.00-22.00, down from $21.00-23.00.
Next-day Four Corners was little changed at $20.20-23.50.
Cash Palo Verde for the balance of November was quoted $22.00-22.60, while COB for November was quoted $23.75-25.00 per MWh. Mid-Columbia for November was quoted $22.00-23.00.
